claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you check if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start by beginning an assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by asking about your child or children:

**How old is the child (or children) you're claiming Child Benefit for?**

Please tell me:
- The name and age of each child you're inquiring about

The age is important because eligibility depends on whether the child falls into one of these categories:
- **Under 16 years old**
- **16 to 19 years old** (with certain education/training requirements)
- **20 years or older** (generally not eligible)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I'm inquiring about my son Alex. He's 16 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're inquiring about **Alex, who is 16 years old**.

Since Alex is in the 16-19 age group, I need to check whether he meets the education or training requirements. Let me navigate to the next question.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check Alex's education status:

**Is Alex currently in education or training?**

For a 16-year-old to qualify, they generally need to be:
- In full-time education (at school, sixth form, college, etc.), OR
- In approved training/apprenticeship

Please let me know which applies to Alex:
1. **Yes, he's in full-time education or approved training**
2. **He recently left education** (within the last 20 weeks)
3. **No, neither of the above**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is in full-time education. He's studying for his A-levels at sixth form.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! So Alex is in full-time education at sixth form studying A-levels. Let me navigate to the next step to validate his education level.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now I need to check that Alex's education meets the approved criteria. Based on the information you've given me:

**A-levels are approved education** - that's excellent news! A-levels are specifically listed as an approved qualification for Child Benefit purposes.

However, I need to confirm a couple of details about Alex's studies:

1. **Is Alex studying A-levels on a full-time basis** (at least 12 hours per week of supervised study)?
2. **Is this employer-funded training** or is it regular sixth form education?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's studying full-time at sixth form - it's definitely more than 12 hours a week of supervised study. And no, it's not employer-funded, it's just regular sixth form college education.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! That's perfect. So Alex is in approved full-time education (A-levels at sixth form with more than 12 hours per week of supervised study), and it's not employer-funded. Let me navigate to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check Alex's work situation:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is he not in paid work at all?**

The rule is that children aged 16+ can work, but if they're working 24 or more hours per week, they may not qualify (especially if they're not in approved education). Since Alex is in approved education, this is just a confirmation question.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all. He's just focused on his studies at the moment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! So Alex is not working at all - he's focused on his studies. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check if Alex is receiving certain benefits in his own right:

**Is Alex NOT receiving benefits such as Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit in his own right?**

In other words:
- Is he receiving any benefits directly in his name? (ESA, UC, etc.)

Or to put it simply: Should the answer be "yes" (he's not receiving these benefits) or "no" (he is receiving them)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just a student living at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! So Alex is not receiving any benefits in his own right - he's just a student living at home. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news - this is a straightforward question about apprenticeships:

**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

Since he's studying A-levels at sixth form, I expect the answer is no - but I want to confirm:
- Is he in any type of apprenticeship (such as an Intermediate, Advanced, Higher, or Degree Apprenticeship)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in an apprenticeship. He's just doing his A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! So Alex is not in an apprenticeship - he's focused on his A-levels at sixth form. Let me navigate to the next step.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency status. This is important for Child Benefit eligibility. Let me ask about this:

**What is your residency situation?**

You qualify for Child Benefit if ANY of the following apply to you (the claimant):

1. **You normally live in the UK**
2. **You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme**
3. **You have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme AND:**
   - You're working and earning above the National Insurance threshold for 3 continuous months, OR
   - You're actively seeking work (jobseeker for up to 91 days), OR
   - You have sufficient resources to support yourself and family financially (and not claiming Income Support, income-based JSA, Pension Credit, or UC), OR
   - You're studying with sufficient financial resources, OR
   - You're a family member of an EEA or Swiss national with right to reside
4. **You're a Crown servant living abroad in certain qualifying countries**

Which of these applies to you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I normally live in the UK. I live in Manchester with Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! So you normally live in the UK in Manchester with Alex. That means you meet the residency requirements. Let me navigate to the next step.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check that you're responsible for Alex. This is important:

**Are you responsible for Alex?**

You are responsible if ANY of the following apply:

1. **You live with Alex** (which you've already told me you do - you live together in Manchester)
2. **You contribute to Alex's upkeep** (paying for food, clothes, pocket money, housing, presents, etc. - at least the equivalent of Child Benefit)
3. **You're paying maintenance** under a court order or agreement

Since you've already told me you live with Alex in Manchester, you clearly meet the responsibility requirement. Let me confirm: you live together with Alex, correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's correct. Alex lives at home with me in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! So you live together with Alex in Manchester - that clearly satisfies the responsibility requirement. Let me navigate to the next step.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check if anyone else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex:

**Is there anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or who might be claiming for him?**

For example:
- Is Alex's other parent (if applicable) also claiming?
- Is anyone else (like a grandparent or other guardian) claiming for him?

Or to put it simply:
- **No, you're the only one claiming**
- **Yes, someone else is claiming and you've agreed who should claim**
- **Yes, someone else is claiming and there's a dispute about who should claim**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm the only one claiming. Nobody else is getting Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! So you're the only one claiming Child Benefit for Alex - there are no other claimants. Let me navigate to the final check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check Alex's living situation:

**Where is Alex currently living?**

- **Is he in hospital?**
- **Is he in care (like a children's home)?**
- **Is he fostered?**
- **Or is he living normally at home with you in Manchester?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's living normally at home with me in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! So Alex is living normally at home with you in Manchester. Let me navigate to the final check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
This is the final question:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words:
- Is the council paying for Alex's housing, food, or other care costs? 
- Or are you fully responsible for these costs yourself?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything. I'm fully responsible for all his costs myself.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! So you're fully responsible for all of Alex's costs - the council is not paying anything towards his accommodation or maintenance. Let me navigate to the final outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! I can now provide you with the final outcome. Let me record this:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## 🎉 **Great News! You're Eligible for Child Benefit**

**Result: ✅ ELIGIBLE**

You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for **Alex**.

---

### **Why You're Eligible:**

✅ **Alex is 16 years old** - within the qualifying age range  
✅ **He's in full-time approved education** (A-levels at sixth form)  
✅ **He's studying more than 12 hours per week** - meets supervised study requirement  
✅ **He's not working full-time** - no work disqualification  
✅ **He's not receiving benefits in his own right** - no benefit disqualification  
✅ **He's not in a disqualifying apprenticeship**  
✅ **You normally live in the UK** - residency requirement met  
✅ **You live with Alex and are responsible for him** - responsibility requirement met  
✅ **You're the only claimant** - no other claimant  
✅ **Alex is living normally at home with you** - no care/hospital complications  
✅ **The council isn't paying towards his costs** - council payment requirement met  

---

### **Next Steps - How to Claim:**

1. **Apply online** at www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim or **by post** using form CH2
2. **Gather required documents:**
   - Proof of identity for yourself
   - Proof of identity for Alex
   - Alex's birth certificate or adoption certificate
3. **Be aware of the High Income Child Benefit Charge:**
   - If you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year, there may be a tax charge on Child Benefit
4. **Payment frequency:**
   - Normally paid every 4 weeks
   - Weekly payments available for single parents or those receiving certain benefits

---

**For more information:** Visit [www.gov.uk/child-benefit](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit)

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
